description:
Allow extensions to register tools and slash-commands at session start, matching
pi-mono's registerTool and registerCommand extension APIs.

Reference: tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/agent-session.ts lines 2030-2231.
Reference: tmp/pi-mono/packages/coding-agent/src/core/extensions/types.ts lines 1066-1292.

Depends on: ExtensionRunner ticket.

## tool_registry and active tools

Session.State already has tool_registry: %{String.t() => Tool.t()} and tools: [Tool.t()].
(tool_registry was added in the Session.State migration ticket.)

Add to session.ex:

  def set_active_tools(pid, tool_names) when is_list(tool_names)
    — replaces state.tools with the Tool structs found in tool_registry for
      the given names (skip names not found, log a warning).
    — rebuilds state.base_system_prompt to include prompt_snippet from active tools.

  def get_active_tool_names(pid) :: [String.t()]

  def register_tool(pid, %Tool{} = tool)
    — adds tool to state.tool_registry keyed by tool.name
    — does NOT automatically activate the tool; caller must call set_active_tools

## command_registry in ExtensionRunner

Add to ExtensionRunner state: commands: %{String.t() => (args :: String.t() -> :ok)}
(keyed by command name without the leading slash).

Add to ExtensionRunner public API:
  register_command/3 — (runner_pid, name, handler_fn)
  get_commands/1     — (runner_pid) -> %{name => handler_fn}

Add to session.ex:
  def get_commands(pid) :: map()
    — returns ExtensionRunner.get_commands(state.extension_runner) or %{} if nil

## session_start hook

The :session_start event is the designated place for extensions to call register_tool
and register_command.

Event type: :session_start
Payload: %{session_manager: sm}
This event is notification-only (return value ignored).

Extensions receive it in on_event(:session_start, payload, ctx) and then call:
  ctx.register_tool.(%Tool{...})
  ctx.register_command.("name", fn args -> ... end)

Add these two action functions to the ctx map passed to extension handlers:
  register_tool:    fn Tool.t() -> :ok end
  register_command: fn name, handler_fn -> :ok end

Both call back into the Session via GenServer.call to update tool_registry and
ExtensionRunner command registry.

## Wire session_start emission

In session.ex init/1, after starting ExtensionRunner and registering all extension
modules, emit:
  Session.emit_hook(self(), :session_start, %{session_manager: state.session_manager})

## Slash-command dispatch

In session.ex prompt/2 handler, before building the User message:
  If the text starts with "/" and get_commands/1 has a matching handler, call
  the handler with the remaining arguments and return without adding a User message.

## Tests

Create apps/octo_pi_agent/test/octo_pi/agent/extension_registration_test.exs.
  - register_tool/2 adds tool to tool_registry
  - set_active_tools/2 with known name populates state.tools
  - session_start fires and extension can register a tool
  - registered tool is found by set_active_tools after session_start
  - register_command adds to ExtensionRunner; get_commands returns it
  - prompt with "/commandname" calls registered handler instead of adding a message
